newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian home affordability improves - survey.
newsitem.headline: Australian home affordability improves - survey.

text.p: Home loan affordability improved for Australians in the March quarter, with the strongest annual growth rate in four years, Citibank and the Real Estate Institute of Australia (REIA) said in a survey on Monday.

The Citibank and REIA quarterly home loan affordability indicator report showed home loan affordability rose 5.1 percent from the December 1996 quarter and 16.7 percent from the corresponding period last year.
This is the seventh consecutive quarterly improvement in affordability and is mainly due to lenders passing on interest rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), it said.

Citibank and REIA survey said median house prices in most states resulted in an increase in the average size of home loans, while falling interest rates meant that average monthly loan repayments fell 4.6 percent to A$845.
The survey said Australians on average pay 24 percent of their income towards meeting the cost of loan repayments, down from 25.2 percent in December 1996 quarter.
The Reserve Bank cut official cash rates by 50 basis points in each of four separate reductions starting in July 1996 to last month. Official cash rates now stand at 5.5 percent.
A majority of economists now expect a fifth rate cut after the release of worse than expected labour force data for May and a run of other weak data.
Economists surveyed by Reuters put the chances of another cut at 60 percent, up from 35 percent two weeks ago.
